sources.title: Rights of way and accessing land: overview
sources.role: Official public overview of rights of way and open-access land.
sources.facts: The overview distinguishes public roads, public rights of way, open-access land, permissive access and possible historic rights.
sources.guard: A general access category does not prove a route exists on a parcel, its legal alignment, width, status, condition or development implications.

sources.title: Use public rights of way
sources.role: Official description of footpaths, bridleways, restricted byways and byways open to all traffic.
sources.facts: The page describes permitted users by right-of-way category and directs users to definitive records and councils.
sources.guard: OS or council mapping alone may not settle the definitive legal line, modification orders, temporary closures, obstructions or private rights.

sources.title: Public rights of way: landowner responsibilities
sources.role: Official guidance on landowner duties where public rights cross land.
sources.facts: Landowners must keep routes visible and avoid obstructing or endangering users; definitive maps are legal records held by relevant authorities.
sources.guard: Guidance does not prove compliance, exact route geometry, maintenance condition, diversion approval or that development can obstruct a route.

sources.title: Open access land: management, rights and responsibilities
sources.role: Official guidance on CROW open-access rights and land management.
sources.facts: CROW access generally applies to mapped open country and registered common land, with specified rights, exclusions and management rules.
sources.guard: Mapped open access does not prove ownership, all access rights, permanent unrestricted access, planning acceptability or development consent.

sources.title: Open access land and coastal margin: restrict public access
sources.role: Official process for access restrictions for management, safety or fire prevention.
sources.facts: Eligible interest holders may apply to the relevant authority for restrictions where statutory grounds are met.
sources.guard: The existence of a restriction process does not prove a restriction is active, approved, correctly mapped or sufficient for construction activity.

sources.title: Public Rights of Way and Common Land
sources.role: Official collection for rights-of-way and common-land casework.
sources.facts: The collection separates common-land works, deregistration, forms, notices, decisions and public-right-of-way order procedures.
sources.guard: A casework collection does not prove a parcel has a pending or decided order, consent, objection, ownership change or extinguishment.

sources.title: Works on Common land and Deregistering Common Land: guidance
sources.role: Official guidance for works and deregistration involving common or village-green land.
sources.facts: Certain works require consent under section 38 of the Commons Act 2006 or other specific statutory routes.
sources.guard: General consent routes do not prove land is registered common, that consent is needed, that an application succeeds or that planning permission exists.

sources.title: Common land and village greens
sources.role: Official public route to local registers and change processes.
sources.facts: Local councils maintain registers describing land, rights and recorded ownership; proposed changes are advertised and may be commented on.
sources.guard: Register summaries do not replace certified register entries, title records, exact boundaries, commoners' rights analysis or proposal-specific consent.

package_guard: Rights-of-way guidance, open-access maps, common-land registers and casework routes do not by themselves prove exact legal alignment, ownership, access restrictions, consent, diversion, extinguishment, planning acceptability, funding or delivery.
